message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether deleting my step brother's profile on my Nintendo Switch was morally acceptable. Let me break this down step by step. First, I made the profile for him because he was really into the Switch, and it helped distract him while I studied. That seems like a good intention. I didn't want him messing up my saves, so creating a separate profile was a practical solution. I guess that's fair because I was using the Switch for my own purposes too. Then, after a while, I got annoyed because every time I wanted to play, I had to switch back to my profile. It was a minor inconvenience, but enough that I decided to delete his profile. That seems a bit selfish, but I didn't think it was a big deal because I usually don't bring the Switch over when I visit. So, I thought he wouldn't be using it much anyway. But then, when I went to my dad's for Thanksgiving, my step brother found out his profile was gone. He was really upset, even cried a little, and now he's shut himself in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knew my step brother was enjoying playing. That makes me feel bad because I didn't consider how much it meant to him. I guess the main issue here is that I didn't communicate with him about deleting the profile. I just did it without telling him, which probably made him feel betrayed or hurt. Even though I thought it was a small thing, it had a big emotional impact on him. So, morally, was it acceptable? I don't think so. Even if I had a reason, not considering his feelings and not talking to him about it was wrong. It's important to respect others' feelings, especially when it comes to things they care about, like their gaming profile. I should have found a better way to handle the inconvenience without just deleting it, maybe by explaining my feelings or finding another solution together.
